subject: mathematics
question_text: If a = 2i + 2j − 3k and b = 3i − 2j + 2k, find the angle between 2a + b and a + 2b.

verification.note: Source: Sri Chaitanya, FAST TRACK IPE for Jr. Students — Mathematics-IA (2026-27 edition), chapter 7 PRODUCT OF VECTORS, Short Answer question 40, book p.75. Only the question was taken. The solution, the step order and the mark split are this answer book's own work — see docs/ORIGINALITY_MATHS.md. Computed twice. Component route, the route on the page: 2a + b = 7i + 2j − 4k and a + 2b = 8i − 2j + k; their dot product is 56 − 4 − 4 = 48; |2a + b| = √(49 + 4 + 16) = √69 and |a + 2b| = √(64 + 4 + 1) = √69; so cos θ = 48/69 = 16/23. Symbolic route, done independently from |a|² = 17, |b|² = 17 and a·b = 6 − 4 − 6 = −4: |2a + b|² = 4(17) + 4(−4) + 17 = 69; |a + 2b|² = 17 + 4(−4) + 4(17) = 69; (2a + b)·(a + 2b) = 2(17) + 5(−4) + 2(17) = 34 − 20 + 34 = 48. Both routes give 48 and 69 twice, so cos θ = 16/23 ≈ 0.6957 and θ = Cos⁻¹(16/23) ≈ 45.92°. The two combined vectors happening to have equal length is a real feature of these numbers, not an arithmetic slip: |a| = |b| = √17, so 2a + b and a + 2b are mirror images of each other. THE MARK SPLIT IS OURS, NOT THE BOOK'S: the Mathematics-IA volume prints no per-step mark allocation on any answer. The 1+1+1+1 split rewards the four separate acts: forming the two combinations, the dot product, the two magnitudes, and the angle. Paper position: Maths-1A Section B runs Q11 to Q18 at 4 marks each, answer any 6 of 8, under the 2026-27 pattern; Product of Vectors carries a Section B slot on the paper and also appears in Section C. This is a coaching publication, not a TSBIE document, so the split stays unverified until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it.

recall_prompt: Say how you would find the angle between two combinations of a and b — name each move in order.

steps.label: Form the two vectors
steps.margin_note: First mark. The angle is between the two COMBINATIONS, not between a and b, so build them in components first. Double each component, do not double only the first one.
steps.memory_tip: Build the two combinations first — the angle is between them, not between a and b.

accept: two a plus b is seven i plus two j minus four k
a plus two b is eight i minus two j plus k
double each vector and add component by component
two a plus b seven i two j minus four k vasthundi
form both combinations before doing anything else

steps.why: The angle formula works on whatever two vectors are named, so the two named combinations have to exist in component form before it can be applied.
common_mistakes: Finding the angle between a and b instead of between the two combinations.
Doubling only the i component when writing 2a.

steps.label: Take their dot product
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Multiply matching components and add, watching the two negative products. Naming the combinations u and v keeps the next two lines short.
steps.memory_tip: Name the two combinations u and v so the formula stays short.
lines: Let u = 2a + b and v = a + 2b.

accept: the dot product is fifty six minus four minus four which is forty eight
u dot v is forty eight
multiply matching components and add
fifty six minus four minus four, forty eight
seven eights are fifty six and then two negatives

steps.why: The dot product is the numerator of the cosine formula and it also fixes the sign of the answer. Here it is positive, so the angle will be acute.
common_mistakes: Adding the two negative terms as +4 each.
Taking a cross product, which does not give an angle directly.

steps.label: Find both magnitudes
steps.margin_note: Third mark. Both come out as √69 — that is genuine here, because |a| and |b| are both √17. Do not simplify √69 further; 69 = 3 × 23 has no square factor.
steps.memory_tip: Both magnitudes are √69 here, so the product underneath is just 69.

accept: both magnitudes are root sixty nine
forty nine plus four plus sixteen is sixty nine
sixty four plus four plus one is also sixty nine
rendu magnitudes root sixty nine same vasthai
the two lengths are equal here

steps.why: The two lengths are equal because a and b have the same length, so swapping their coefficients produces a mirror image. That equality makes the denominator a whole number and the arithmetic short.
common_mistakes: Deciding the two equal magnitudes must be a slip and changing one of them; the equality is genuine here.

steps.label: Find the angle
steps.margin_note: Last mark. √69 × √69 = 69, so the fraction is 48/69, which cancels by 3 to 16/23. That is not a standard cosine, so leave the exact answer as an inverse cosine.
lines: Let θ be the angle between u and v.

recall.must_convey: That cos θ = 48/69 = 16/23, so θ = Cos⁻¹(16/23), about 46°.
accept: cos theta is forty eight over sixty nine which cancels to sixteen over twenty three
the angle is cos inverse sixteen by twenty three
root sixty nine times root sixty nine is sixty nine
forty eight by sixty nine, cancel cheste sixteen by twenty three
the angle is about forty six degrees

steps.why: The product of the two square roots is the number itself, which removes every root from the answer. A positive cosine below 1 confirms an acute angle, matching the positive dot product found earlier.
common_mistakes: Leaving 48/69 uncancelled, which is not wrong but loses the simplest form.
